how_to_obtain.instruction: Check Amavis configuration for MIME normalization and validation settings
how_to_obtain.expected_output: MIME normalization enabled via $normalize_originating_headers or equivalent setting set to a non-zero/true value; relevant checks not commented out

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check SpamAssassin or Rspamd configuration for MIME structure checks and invalid MIME scoring rules
how_to_obtain.expected_output: MIME-related rules active with scores assigned; MIME_BOUNDARY_DOUBLE_DASH, MIME_HTML_MOSTLY, or similar rule hits visible in test output; absence of MIME rules indicates validation is minimal

how_to_obtain.instruction: Send a test email with a deliberately malformed MIME structure (mismatched boundary) to the server and observe whether it is rejected, quarantined, or delivered
how_to_obtain.command:
swaks --to postmaster@example.com --server mail.example.com --data - <<'EOF'
From: test@external.com
To: postmaster@example.com
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary="boundary1"

--boundary2
Content-Type: text/plain

Mismatched boundary test
--boundary1--
EOF
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SMTP rejection (5xx) or bounce indicating malformed MIME detected; if delivered without rejection, MIME validation is likely not enforced

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the email gateway or security appliance management interface for MIME inspection or message normalization policy settings
how_to_obtain.navigation: Proofpoint: Admin Console > Email Protection > Policies > Content Rules > MIME validation. Mimecast: Administration Console > Gateway > Policies > Content Examination. Exchange Online: Security & Compliance > Anti-malware > Advanced options > enable zero-hour auto purge and MIME inspection
how_to_obtain.expected_output: MIME validation or message normalization shown as enabled with action set to quarantine or reject for malformed structures; disabled state means the control is absent

option_description: Controls the level of anti-malware scanning integrated at the MTA layer for email attachments. Determines whether the mail server inspects attachments using no scanning, signature-based detection only, or full heuristic/behavioral analysis via engines such as ClamAV (via Amavis or clamav-milter) or a commercial gateway scanner.
security_impact: Directly triggers the 'attachment_and_content_filtering_disabled' exposure in the Rego policy. If set to 'none', the policy fires unconditionally. If set to anything other than 'full', the policy also fires when MIME structure validation is absent, meaning partial scanning still leaves the server exposed to novel or obfuscated malware payloads delivered via email attachments (T1027.009, T1027.006).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check whether Amavis is installed and active as the integration bridge between the MTA and ClamAV.
how_to_obtain.command: systemctl status amavis amavisd-new clamav-daemon 2>/dev/null; postconf -n | grep -E 'content_filter|smtpd_milters|non_smtpd_milters'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Active service status lines for amavis/clamav-daemon, and content_filter or milter directives referencing amavisfeed or clamav-milter in Postfix output.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Amavis configuration to determine whether ClamAV is enabled and whether heuristic scanning is active.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Presence of '@av_scanners' with ClamAV entries and absence of 'bypass_virus_checks_maps' with permissive values; heuristic scanner entries indicate 'full' integration.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check for clamav-milter integration directly in the MTA without Amavis as middleware.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Milter socket paths referencing clamav-milter and an active service state confirm direct milter integration.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the mail server administrator or review change management records to determine if a commercial gateway scanner (e.g., Sophos, McAfee Email Gateway) is positioned upstream of this MTA and whether heuristic/behavioral scanning is licensed and enabled.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documentation confirming a scanning appliance with heuristic detection enabled upstream, or confirmation that no scanning is in place.

option_description: Indicates whether the MTA performs reverse DNS (PTR) lookup validation on the IP address of each connecting SMTP client before accepting mail. When enabled, the MTA queries DNS for a PTR record matching the client IP and may take action based on the result.
security_impact: One of two conditions triggering the 'dns_reverse_lookup_validation_absent' exposure. When false, the Rego policy fires immediately, flagging the absence of any PTR-based friction against spam and phishing sources using ephemeral or dynamically allocated IP infrastructure (T1568.001, T1590.002). Even when true, the exposure still fires unless 'no_ptr_rejection_policy' is set to 'reject'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Postfix, check smtpd_client_restrictions for PTR validation directives.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output containing 'reject_unknown_client_hostname' or 'reject_unknown_reverse_client_hostname' confirms PTR validation is configured; absence means it is not.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Exim, inspect the ACL configuration for reverse host lookup verification conditions.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ACL stanzas containing 'verify = reverse_host_lookup' confirm PTR validation is active in Exim.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Sendmail, check the ResolverOptions and any ruleset that invokes DNS lookups for connecting clients.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Sendmail ResolverOptions with relevant flags or FEATURE macros enabling DNS-based client checks indicate PTR validation is enabled.

option_description: Defines the action the MTA takes when a connecting client IP has no matching PTR (reverse DNS) record. Options are to reject the connection outright, tag/flag the message for downstream scoring, or silently accept it with no action taken.
security_impact: The second condition in the 'dns_reverse_lookup_validation_absent' Rego rule. Even when 'ptr_validation_enabled' is true, if this policy is 'accept' or 'tag', the exposure still fires, because neither outcome creates a reliable barrier against spam or phishing senders using infrastructure without PTR records (T1568.001). Only a value of 'reject' satisfies the policy check.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Postfix, determine whether the PTR check directive causes a hard reject or is used in a milter/policy service that only tags messages.
how_to_obtain.command: postconf -n smtpd_client_restrictions | grep -E 'reject_unknown|warn_if_reject|check_client_access'; postconf -n smtpd_soft_error_limit smtpd_error_sleep_time
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 'reject_unknown_reverse_client_hostname' without a preceding 'warn_if_reject' modifier indicates hard rejection. 'warn_if_reject' before the check means tagging/logging only.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check SpamAssassin, Rspamd, or Amavis integration to determine if missing PTR records only contribute to a spam score rather than causing rejection.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Rules referencing RDNS_NONE with score assignments (rather than reject actions) confirm a 'tag' policy; hard reject rules or 'reject_symbol' entries in Rspamd indicate 'reject'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Exim, review the ACL action associated with the reverse_host_lookup verify condition to determine whether it denies or warns.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An 'deny' verb following the verify condition confirms 'reject'; 'warn' or 'add_header' verbs confirm 'tag'; no condition present confirms 'accept'.

option_description: Indicates whether the mail spool or queue directory (e.g., /var/spool/mqueue for Sendmail, /var/spool/postfix for Postfix) has world-write permission (mode includes o+w), allowing any local OS user to write files into it regardless of their group membership.
security_impact: Directly triggers the 'mail_queue_directory_permission_misconfiguration' exposure in the Rego policy when true. World-writable queue directories allow any local user to inject forged or malicious messages into the mail queue, tamper with queued messages before delivery, or stage data for exfiltration via the email channel (T1098.002, T1114.002).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the octal permission mode of the Postfix queue directories for world-write bits.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Permission octets with a '2', '3', '6', or '7' in the last (others) position indicate world-write. Secure directories typically show 700 or 710.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the Sendmail mail queue directory for world-write permissions.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Permissions of 700 or 750 are expected. Any mode ending in 2, 3, 6, or 7 (others write bit set) is a finding.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use find to scan all queue-related paths for world-writable directories across common MTA variants.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No output is the expected secure result. Any directory path returned is world-writable and constitutes a finding.

option_description: Records the OS username that owns the mail queue or spool directory. The owner should be the dedicated MTA service account (e.g., postfix, mail, smmsp, mailnull, exim, or qmail). Ownership by root or a general-purpose account with broad group membership increases injection risk when combined with permissive directory modes.
security_impact: Used in the 'mail_queue_directory_permission_misconfiguration' Rego rule, which fires if the owner is not in the set ['postfix', 'mail', 'smmsp', 'mailnull', 'exim', 'qmail']. Root ownership combined with loose permissions is particularly dangerous because it widens the blast radius of any local privilege escalation—an attacker who compromises any root-equivalent path gains write access to the mail queue (T1098.002, T1114.002).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Retrieve the owning username of all primary MTA queue directories using stat.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each path should be owned by its respective MTA service account (e.g., 'postfix /var/spool/postfix'). Output showing 'root' or any general user account is a finding.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Cross-reference the directory owner against the user defined in the MTA configuration to confirm alignment.
how_to_obtain.command: postconf -n queue_directory mail_owner 2>/dev/null; stat -c '%U' $(postconf -h queue_directory 2>/dev/null || echo '/var/spool/postfix')
how_to_obtain.expected_output: The username returned by stat should match the value of Postfix's 'mail_owner' directive (default: 'postfix').

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Sendmail, check the RunAsUser parameter and compare to the spool directory owner.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: RunAsUser should match the owner shown by stat (typically 'smmsp' or 'mail'). A mismatch or root ownership is a finding.

option_description: Indicates whether the mail queue directory has group-write permission (g+w) AND the owning group includes members other than the MTA service account. This condition allows any local user who is a member of that group to write to the queue directory, even if they are not the MTA service account itself.
security_impact: Directly triggers the 'mail_queue_directory_permission_misconfiguration' Rego exposure when true. Group-write with a broadly-membered group is functionally equivalent to world-write for any group member, enabling message injection or tampering in the queue (T1098.002, T1114.002). This is a common misconfiguration on systems where administrators add users to the 'mail' group for convenience without recognizing the queue write risk.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the group-write bit on the queue directory and identify the owning group name.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A '6' or '7' in the middle (group) position of the octal mode (e.g., 770, 760) indicates group-write is set. Note the group name for membership inspection.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate all members of the owning group to determine whether non-MTA users are present.
how_to_obtain.command: QDIR_GROUP=$(stat -c '%G' /var/spool/postfix 2>/dev/null || stat -c '%G' /var/spool/mqueue 2>/dev/null); echo "Queue group: $QDIR_GROUP"; getent group "$QDIR_GROUP"
how_to_obtain.expected_output: The group entry should list only the MTA service account (or be empty beyond the primary user). Any additional OS users in the group combined with g+w on the queue directory constitutes a finding.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check for users with supplementary group membership in the queue directory's owning group beyond the MTA account.
how_to_obtain.command: QDIR_GROUP=$(stat -c '%G' /var/spool/postfix 2>/dev/null || echo 'mail'); getent passwd | awk -F: '{print $1}' | xargs -I{} sh -c 'groups {} 2>/dev/null | grep -q "'"$QDIR_GROUP"'" && echo {}' | grep -v -E '^(postfix|mail|smmsp|mailnull|exim|qmail)$'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No output is the expected result. Any username printed indicates a non-MTA user with group membership that could be leveraged if g+w is set on the queue directory.
